title: Godown
logline: Branch B, the twenty-five minutes after the line goes dead: Nandini walks into Bhaiyaji's godown with only Pushpa behind her, finds a confession laid out for Nirala to sign, and answers it with a seizure memo spoken aloud, item by item, until her own SHO is item six and the DSP is sending a force. Then Tripathi learns whose phone was in the fake inspector's pocket.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; names, 'sahab', 'ji', 'madam', 'thana', 'godown', 'tamasha' and 'aaiye' kept as spoken in India.

characters.name: Nandini Joshi
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, Imlipur thana, six weeks into her first posting. Tonight she broke the DSP's order to send Nirala in; now she goes in after him with no order and no backup.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed, long neck. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, a firm mouth. Black hair, clean centre parting, low ponytail to the shoulder blades; no fringe, no loose strands. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. Approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt with two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip (the cuffs are in it); black shoes; blue ballpoint pen in her left chest pocket. Nirala's brass medal is buttoned inside that same left chest pocket, out of sight. No cap, no stars. A printed memo pad, folded, in her right trouser pocket from b1 until she takes it out in b6. Cherry-red helmet: left on the stall bench in b1; no helmet from b2 on (D-016 direction 19). Her notebook: on the bench in b1 Shot 1, in Pushpa's knitting bag from b1 Shot 2. HANDS: b6 to b9, the printed memo pad with carbon paper (painted blank) and the blue pen; after l19 the pink slip is tucked under the pad's top sheet; from b8 her own plain black smartphone in her LEFT hand (held against the back of the pad while she writes in b9). b10: pad, with the slip under its top sheet, into her right trouser pocket, pen back in her left chest pocket; phone in her left hand at her left ear. b11 and b12: wooden revolver in her RIGHT hand, barrel to the floor, in profile; phone still in her left hand.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Indian English with a neutral, educated small-city north-Indian accent; not British, not American. Keeps 'madam', 'thana', 'sahab' and 'ji'. Under pressure the whole episode, so quieter, slower and more exact, never louder. The one exception is l11, through the steel shutter: projected to carry, not shouted. The memo items (l14 to l25) are dictation: level, unhurried, each word placed, as if for a witness. Dry, not sarcastic.

characters.name: Sudhir Nirala
characters.role: The man who ran the fake thana. Shut inside the godown since midnight, found out, and frightened.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, neat black pencil moustache. PERIOD 1b (as Nandini dressed him in s2b01): the home-stitched copy of the force uniform, one size too big, but with the shoulder seams squared, the sleeve cuffs folded back so his hands show, and the belt pulled tight with its tail tucked in. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars; lantern sleeve patches. The only peaked cap in the series (khaki, teal band, shiny black peak, no badge), dead level, never taken off. NO MEDAL: there is a bare patch of shirt above his left chest pocket. Brown leather holster on his right hip: holds the wooden revolver in b2; empty from b3 on. Nandini's phone is NOT in his pocket in this episode: it lies face down on a sack beside him until b8.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, forty, light careful tenor. Careful, slightly old-fashioned Indian English as learnt from manuals ('incorrect', 'minimum two persons'), with a small-town north-Indian accent; not British, not American. No contractions. Courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes: the comedy is that he means it. Frightened tonight: a thin, steady voice, not a stammer. In b7 he gives the count like a munshi, calmer for having a job to do.

characters.name: Balram 'Bhaiyaji' Thakur
characters.role: Antagonist. Owns the godown and the eight hundred sacks. Has the fake inspector where he wants him, until the real one knocks.
characters.look: Indian man, 45, broad and solid, about 178 cm, thick neck, big square hands. Brown skin, thick black hair combed straight back, full black moustache, an unhurried closed-lip smile as his resting face. Spotless white cotton kurta, sleeves pushed up the forearms, white pyjama trousers, brown leather sandals. Heavy gold watch on his LEFT wrist. Dark sunglasses pushed up on top of his head, never over his eyes. A fat ring of godown keys hooked on his RIGHT index finger, swinging. In b11 the smile is gone for the first time in the series.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, mid-forties, warm, low, smiling voice. Soft, hospitable Indian English with a small-town north-Indian accent; not British, not American. Keeps 'Tripathi ji', 'sahab' and 'aaiye'. Courteous to the point of menace; never threatens, never hurries, laughs before he says the worst thing (l20). Under pressure the smile leaves the voice and nothing replaces it: flat and quiet (l30).

characters.name: Pushpa Kumari
characters.role: Head Constable, twenty-six years at the Imlipur thana. Her keypad phone holds the only recording of the night.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with two steel knitting needles crossed through it. Approved force uniform with ONE off-white bar on teal epaulettes, lantern patches, khaki trousers, black shoes. Over it a hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan, open, two sagging pockets; a ball of orange wool in the right pocket. Cloth knitting bag over her left shoulder (Nandini's notebook in it from b1 Shot 2). Her old keypad phone in its knitted orange cover in her hand in b1, then in her left cardigan pocket. The truck key goes into her right pocket, with the wool, in b8 (heard, not shown).
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Plain, unhurried Indian English with a small-town north-Indian accent, short sentences; not British, not American. Keeps 'madam'. Never surprised; warmth shows only as dryness. Under pressure slower and more exact.

characters.name: Dayashankar Tripathi
characters.role: SHO, Imlipur. Signed the truck's movement slip this evening. Arrives at half past twelve to arrest a gang and finds himself in the memo.
characters.look: Indian man, 56, large, heavy and slow, about 175 cm, a big soft belly straining his shirt. Warm-brown skin, bald dome with a fringe of grey hair at the sides, heavy jowls, clean-shaven, half-closed sleepy eyes. Approved force uniform worn slack: khaki half-sleeve shirt with the top two buttons open over a white vest, teal epaulettes with three off-white bars, lantern sleeve patches, khaki trousers. Red-and-white checked gamchha over his LEFT shoulder. Paper cone of roasted peanuts in his left hand. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, mid-fifties, deep, slow, comfortable baritone. Slow Indian English with a strong Eastern-UP accent, never crisp; Hindi words kept ('tamasha'); not British, not American. Arrives lazy and irritated, with a sigh (l23). Under pressure he does not shout: he stops chewing, goes flat and low, and then blames someone (l31, l32).

characters.name: Anil Rathore, DSP
characters.role: The sub-division's DSP. Voice on the phone only in this episode.
characters.look: Not seen in this episode. Voice only.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, late forties, bright, quick, clipped baritone. Fluent officer's Indian English, brisk; not British, not American. Phone-filtered (narrow band, slight line hiss), kept wide enough that every consonant survives. Under pressure he pauses once, then pivots: here the pause is before his only line, which is brisk and level. He takes nothing back.

location: Two of the seven series plates: crossing_stall (b1) and godown (b2 to b12). Fictional town of Imlipur; the godown's dark front is in sight of the stall across the railway line. All night, no crowd.
time_of_day: Night: about 12:12 a.m. in b1; a quarter past twelve at the shutter (b4); 12:20 at the memo (b6, spoken); half past twelve when Tripathi arrives (b9, spoken); about 12:35 for the DSP call (b10). Neither plate has a clock; every time that matters is spoken.

beats.action: OPENS ON A SOUND: the flat tone of a dead line, on frame one, from Pushpa's keypad phone. Crossing stall, night, one hanging bulb, the signal lamp. Shot 1 (the hook, wide): Nandini already walking away from the bench across the single track, toward the small black mouth of the godown up the dark road; on the bench behind her, the cherry-red helmet and her notebook beside it, left where she sat; her blue pen is clipped in her left chest pocket. Shot 2 (two-shot on the track, Nandini picture-left striding, Pushpa picture-right a step behind, knitting bag on her shoulder with Nandini's notebook now sticking out of its mouth, scooped off the bench as she followed, and the keypad phone in its orange cover still in her hand): l01 and l02 play over it. Pushpa drops the phone into her cardigan pocket on l02.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [quietly] Force, madam?

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] You're with me.

beats.action: Inside the godown, under one bare bulb on a long wire. Shot 1 (single, Nirala): he sits very upright on a jute sack, cap dead level, hands flat on his knees; beside him on the sack, Nandini's black phone lies face down. Over the silence. Shot 2 (insert): Bhaiyaji's square hand, key ring swinging from the index finger, lays one typed sheet (painted blank) and a pen across it on the platform of the green weighing scale; l03 plays over it. Shot 3 (two-shot, Bhaiyaji picture-left standing over the scale, Nirala picture-right on his sack; behind them the fully loaded truck under its grey tarpaulin, tailgate up): l05. Shot 4 (close, Bhaiyaji, smiling): l06.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [calm] 'Fake police gang looted government grain. Ringleader: Sudhir Nirala.'

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [calm] Tripathi ji is on his way, to arrest you.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [quietly] All DSP sahab needs is one arrest.

beats.action: Two set-ups over the silence (about 0.8 s each), then the lines. Shot 1 (insert, in profile): Bhaiyaji's fingers have unbuttoned the holster flap on Nirala's hip and lifted the wooden revolver out, held flat in profile, barrel to picture-left, pointing at nothing. Shot 2 (insert): the revolver lying on its side on the scale platform beside the typed sheet; the dial needle has hardly moved. A knock of wood on jute is heard between the two shots. Shot 3 (close, Nirala): he has picked up the sheet in both shaking hands and is reading it, eyes on the page, not on Bhaiyaji; l07. Shot 4 (tighter on Nirala, the edge of the sheet trembling in the foreground): l08. Shot 5 (close, Nirala): the sheet laid back on the scale, the pen across it, unsigned; his eyes go to the face-down phone on the sack beside him; l09 under his breath.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [nervous] The date here is incorrect, Bhaiyaji.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] And a 'gang' requires minimum two persons.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [whispers] The tea has gone cold.

beats.action: Three heavy blows on the steel shutter from outside, over the silence (order per D-016 direction 13: the blows, Bhaiyaji's smile, then her voice). Shot 1 (close, Bhaiyaji): he turns his head toward the shutter and smiles; l10. Shot 2 (wide from inside, the shutter mouth closed, a line of night under it; Nirala small on his sack in the foreground, his face turned to the shutter): l11, Nandini's voice through the steel, projected to carry, not shouted. Bhaiyaji crosses toward the shutter (seen only as his white back at frame edge).

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [calm] Tripathi ji is here.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] Police. Open the shutter.

beats.action: The shutter rattles up (one frame plus sound). Shot 1 (from inside, low): the open shutter mouth, and in it Nandini in full uniform, straight as a post in the spill of the bulb, no helmet, with Pushpa one step behind her at picture-right; held over the silence. Shot 2 (close, Bhaiyaji, the smile back in one breath, the key ring swinging): l12. Shot 3 (two-shot, Bhaiyaji picture-left waving an open palm like a host toward Nirala, who sits small on his sack picture-right): l13.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [laughs] Madam! Aaiye. Good that you have come.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [calm] I caught a fake Inspector for you. Take him.

beats.action: Her look, over the silence, as three stills of about 0.8 s each. Shot 1 (single): Nirala on his sack. Shot 2 (wide): the green scale with the wooden revolver on its platform in the foreground, the loaded truck under its tarpaulin behind it. Shot 3 (close, insert): her hands taking the printed memo pad (painted blank, carbon paper under the top sheet; ov_memo_head) out of her right trouser pocket and clicking the blue pen from her left chest pocket; the click is heard. Shot 4 (single, Nandini, writing, eyes on the pad): l14. Shot 5 (close, Bhaiyaji, hearing his full name, the keys stop swinging): l15. Shot 6 (close, Nirala): he understands what she is doing; his hands come off his knees; l16 plays over him, Pushpa's voice from off frame.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Seizure memo. Time: twelve twenty at night.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Godown of Balram Thakur.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] Witness: Head Constable Pushpa Kumari.

beats.action: Item by item, one still each. Shot 1 (insert): a jute sack with its blank stencil patch, her hand flat on it; l17. Shot 2 (single, Nirala on his sack, sitting up like a munshi, counting off the truck with his eyes): l18; she writes item two from his count. Shot 3 (insert): the pink movement slip (painted blank, ov_slip_signature) on the scale beside the unsigned sheet and the revolver, her fingers lifting it; Shot 4 (single, Nandini reading it): l19; after it she tucks the slip under the pad's top sheet. Shot 5 (close, Bhaiyaji, pleasant, the keys swinging again): l20. Shot 6 (single, Nandini, not looking up from the pad, pen moving): l21.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Item one: sacks with the government stamp.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Eight hundred, madam. All in the truck.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Item three: movement slip. Signed by SHO Tripathi.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [chuckles] Madam, you are alone.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] Item four: owner, present on the spot.

beats.action: Shot 1 (two-shot, Nandini picture-left holding out her open left hand toward the truck cab, pad and pen in her right; Bhaiyaji picture-right, not moving): l22. Then over the silence, three inserts of about 0.8 s each: Shot 2 (insert): Pushpa's hand taking the truck's own key out of the cab door (the clink of it dropping into her wool-filled pocket is heard over the next shot, not shown). Shot 3 (insert): Nandini's left hand lifting her own black phone off the sack, screen still dark. Shot 4 (close, Bhaiyaji): his eyes on the phone; the beat ends on his look.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Item five: key of the truck. Seized.

beats.action: Headlights sweep across the sacks through the open shutter, over the silence (an engine stopping, a door). Shot 1 (single, Tripathi in the shutter mouth, gamchha on his left shoulder, peanut cone in his left hand, a shell half-cracked in the other; he has come to arrest a gang): l23. Shot 2 (single, Nandini, writing, she does not look up; the phone held against the back of the pad in her left hand, the pen in her right): l24. Shot 3 (close, Tripathi, chewing stopped): l25 plays over his face. Five principals are in the room; no frame holds more than two faces (D-016 direction 14).

lines.speaker: tripathi
lines.text: [sighs] What tamasha is this, Joshi?

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] Item six: SHO Dayashankar Tripathi.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Twelve thirty at night, present on the spot.

beats.action: Shot 1 (single, Nandini, over the silence, keypad tones and one ring): before dialling she slides the memo pad, the slip under its top sheet, into her right trouser pocket and clips the pen back in her left chest pocket; her left thumb is on the phone. Shot 2 (close, Nandini, phone at her left ear, back of the phone to camera): l26. Shot 3 (a second framing of Nandini, tighter, three-quarter profile, so the cut separates the takes): l27. Shot 4 (close, Tripathi, peanut cone lowered, not chewing): l28, her voice, plays over him. Shot 5 (insert, in the 0.8 s pause on the line, the room's reaction to 'Force भेजिए।'): Bhaiyaji's hand, the key ring hanging still from his finger. Then the DSP's voice over Shot 6 (close, Nandini, listening): l29. He takes nothing back: his order and his 'उसी FIR में' stand.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] DSP sahab, SI Joshi. It is no longer about the fake thana's phone.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Bhaiyaji's voice is on record, and eight hundred sacks are in my memo.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] Send the force.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [calm] Twenty minutes.

beats.action: Shot 1 (two-shot): Bhaiyaji seated on a sack picture-left, the smile gone for the first time in the series, sunglasses still up on his head, nodding at the black phone in Nandini's left hand (off frame); Tripathi standing picture-right, looking down at him: l30. Then over the silence: Shot 2 (two-shot, Nirala picture-left, unasked, holding the wooden revolver out across his body BUTT FIRST, in profile, barrel pointing at the floor; Nandini picture-right taking it by the grip with her right hand, the phone still in her left). Never pointed at a face or at the camera. The beat ends as a dry peanut shell cracks in Tripathi's fist, off frame.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [flatly] Madam's phone came out of his pocket, Tripathi ji. Do something.

beats.action: ENDING, SPOKEN. Shot 1 (close, Tripathi, crushed shell in his right fist, his eyes moving from Nirala to the phone in Nandini's hand to her): l31. Shot 2 (single, Tripathi, his arm out, pointing at her with one finger, a finger only): l32. Shot 3 (close, Nandini, front on): the wooden revolver in her right hand at her side, barrel to the floor, in profile (or out of frame); her left hand, still holding the phone, comes to rest flat over the buttoned left chest pocket where the medal is. Hold on her face over the silence. Nirala's face appears once, in Shot 1's eyeline, as a single insert if S4 wants it.

lines.speaker: tripathi
lines.text: [flatly] So it was madam who sent him in.

lines.speaker: tripathi
lines.text: [quietly] In court, I will say this: madam knew everything.

sfx_notes: b1: on frame one, the flat continuous tone of a dead line from Pushpa's keypad phone, close and thin, alone for the first half-second; it keeps going under l01 and is cut by a key click as the phone goes into her pocket on l02. Night bed at the crossing: crickets, the signal relay ticking, footsteps on railway ballast (long even strides, short brisk steps). No train.
Bed, b2 to b12: the godown at night: a high tin roof ticking as it cools, one bare bulb humming on its wire, a faint jute rustle. Low, so every line sits clear of it.
b2: paper laid on steel; a pen rolling to a stop. The key ring jingles softly under l05, never over a word.

b3: a leather flap unbuttoning; one dull knock of wood on jute between shots 1 and 2; the scale's needle gives one small spring creak. Paper trembling under l07 and l08. Nothing at all under l09: it is under his breath and must stay intelligible.

b4: three heavy blows on the steel shutter, booming and ringing, all of them before l10. l11 is Nandini through steel, projected (not shouted) so it carries: muffle it lightly, keep it intelligible, and leave the ring of the third blow fully decayed before she speaks.
b5: the shutter rattling up, loud and long; it must have stopped dead a full beat before l12 begins. Night air and crickets come in through the open mouth.
b6: a ballpoint pen click, dry and close, on the pad insert (Shot 3) before l14; pen on carbon paper under l14 to l16, quiet. The key ring stops jingling on l15.
b7: a palm on jute (l17); the slip's paper rustle as she lifts it (before l19, not under it); pen scratch between items.
b8: after l22: the truck key slid out of the cab door lock; a soft clink as it drops into a wool-filled pocket (the only telling of the pocket: no insert); the phone lifted off jute.
b9: headlight sweep as a low electrical hum; an engine idling and cutting out; a car door; slow heavy footsteps; a peanut shell cracking once before l23. Everything settles before l24.

b10: keypad tones, one ring, the click of pick-up, all over Shot 1. The DSP (l29) is phone-filtered (narrow band, faint line hiss), kept wide enough that consonants survive; the bed ducks right down under it and nothing else plays on it. Her lines are unfiltered.
b11: a sack creaking as Bhaiyaji settles, just before l30; the revolver's light wooden knock against her palm. A dry peanut shell crushed in a fist at the end of the silence, as a pre-lap into b12.
b12: l31 and l32 sit on almost nothing: the bed ducks to the bulb hum alone under l32, the cliffhanger, so every word is clear. After l32, near silence for the hold.
music_note: No music in b1 to b5: the dead tone, the walk and the godown play on sound alone, and the shutter rattle is the loudest thing in the episode. From the pen click in b6 a light, dry plucked figure (the series' caper motif, slowed) enters very quietly and builds a little, item by item, through b7 and b8. It stops dead on Tripathi's headlights in b9. b10 is unscored. From l30 in b11 one low sustained string note enters and holds under b12; it drops away under l32 so the line is exposed, and returns for the final hold, unresolved. Instrumental, no melody line over dialogue, no percussion hits.
ending_question: Tripathi will tell the court that she sent the fake inspector in knowing what he was: when she is asked, will she lie, keep her uniform and let Nirala fall alone, or say she sent him and fall with him?
writer_notes: English adaptation (S5) of content/series2/episodes/s2b02/script.hi.json, not a literal translation. Same beats, speakers, line ids (l01 to l03, l05 to l32; l04 stays retired), order, emotion tags and tag positions, and the same silent_seconds and silent_position per beat. action, on_screen, location, sfx_notes, music_note and ending_question are copied unchanged, because picture, sound and music are shared between the two language cuts. In b10's action the reaction insert is to l28, which in this cut is 'Send the force.'; the Hindi quotations in that action are left as written.

Registers follow the bible's English voice notes (content/series2/bible.json, characters[].voice_note.en): Nandini neutral educated Indian English with 'sahab', 'thana', 'madam'; Nirala manual English with no contractions ('incorrect', 'requires minimum two persons'); Bhaiyaji soft and hospitable, keeping 'Tripathi ji', 'sahab' and 'aaiye'; Pushpa plain and short; Tripathi slow, with 'tamasha' kept; the DSP brisk. The D-006 and D-016 rules carried over: the full name Balram Thakur is spoken only in the memo (l15); nobody says a bare 'sahab'; item four and item six share 'present on the spot', so the SHO is filed exactly like the owner; the danger line is said after the call is dead, under his breath (l09).

One word per object, kept across the cut: 'sacks' for बोरी (l17, l27), 'truck', 'movement slip' and 'signed' (l19), 'key' (l22), 'Seizure memo' (l14, matching the bible's English overlay text 'Seizure Memo' for ov_memo_head), 'force' (l01, l28), 'fake' for नक़ली (l03, l13, l26), 'thana' never 'police station'.

Cross-episode phrases for the S5 adapters of other episodes (none of their script.en.json files exist yet, so these are proposals they should match or override in one place): the danger line 'चाय ठंडी हो गई' is 'The tea has gone cold.' (planted in s2b01 b5, paying off the bible's 'First tea, then complaint.'); the s2e03 b6 echo 'नक़ली थाने के phone' is 'the fake thana's phone' (l26); s2a01 b6 reads the same slip as 'Signed by SHO Tripathi.'

Lines that are not word-for-word, and why: l02 'आप हैं ना।' is 'You're with me.' (the Hindi tag 'ना' is dropped, as in the proof, because an English voice misreads 'na'; the meaning is 'you are the force'). l13 adds 'for you': Bhaiyaji offers Nirala like a host handing over a gift, which the open-palm still shows. l14 and l25 say the times as 'twelve twenty at night' and 'twelve thirty at night', the Indian English for रात बारह बजकर बीस and रात साढ़े बारह, and keep the two memo times parallel. l15 and l22 use the memo's 'godown of Balram Thakur', 'key of the truck' order so the name and the object land last. l31 'So it was madam who sent him in.' is longer than 'So madam sent him in.' on purpose: the plain version would run about 2.2 s against the Hindi's 3.3 s and lose the slow arrival of the thought in Tripathi's voice.

Timing (hand estimate, no tool, nothing voiced). Targets are sized to the English, not copied from the Hindi, using the measured Gate 0b English v4 pace from content/proof/flat2d/voice/manifest.jsonl: about 12 to 13.5 characters a second on ordinary lines, a floor of about 1.2 s on one-or-two-word turns. Dictation (l14 to l25), Tripathi and the whisper are sized slower, about 9.5 to 11 a second. Spoken targets add up to 108.9 s against the Hindi's 112.8 s; every line is within 15 per cent of its Hindi target (range 90 to 111 per cent). Plus 18 speaker changes at 0.3 s (5.4 s) and the same 15.7 s of beat silences plus the 0.8 s line pause before l29 (16.5 s): target_total_seconds 130.8. English dialogue is about 1,150 characters without tags (hand count, likely error a few per cent), about 10.6 characters a second overall. Gate 0b measured real v4 takes 20 to 60 per cent over target, worst on short and emotional lines; no line was lengthened to fill a shot. If the English cut runs over 135 s, use the Hindi file's cut order (b12 hold, b9 silence, l10, fold l15 into l14, l08).

Shot fit against the Hindi targets: shortest are l19 (-0.6 s), then l05, l14, l30 and l32 (-0.4 s each); longest are l17 and l18 (+0.3 s each). Shots follow the voice (D-014 rule 6), so the edit absorbs these; no line was padded to match.
